results.title: Digital Engineering for Cubesats With Semantic Web Technologies
results.abstract: Digital Engineering (DE) and the digital thread, which integrates information across the system lifecycle, offer transformative opportunities for systems engineering. This paper explores the application of DE principles to cubesat design and development, leveraging the Digital Engineering Factory (DEF) developed at the University of Arizona. The DEF integrates data from multiple engineering tools into a cohesive dataset using the Violet tool, which organizes the data as a graph database aligned with the University of Arizona Ontology Stack (UAOS). We extend prior work by applying the DEF to a cubesat design project. In particular, we develop a Python-based analysis to simulate orbital decay and calculate the time required for the cubesat to deorbit. This analysis uses inputs from multiple sources and is integrated into the workflow to demonstrate how the DEF supports automated traceability and checking of consistency, correctness, and completeness. This paper details the DEF's architecture, the cubesat application, and key findings, providing a pathway for advancing DE practices in cubesat design and development. Limitations and future research directions are discussed to guide further development of semantic web technologies in DE.

results.title: Digitally-assisted Development of a Space Robotic Arm for Small Satellites Applications
results.abstract: In-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing (ISAM) expands space-based capabilities by extending satellite lifespans and decoupling spacecraft design from launch vehicle constraints. Robotic systems are proposed to support multiple aspects of ISAM missions, from capture and manipulation to manufacturing and repair. Consequently, the rapid development and testing of diverse robotic platforms is imperative to meet the evolving demands of the new space enterprise. This paper proposes a digital engineering framework to expedite the design, development, testing, and operation analysis of space robotic platforms. Digital engineering design tools are employed to optimize design for space environment operations; additionally, traditional manufacturing methods are streamlined with integrated wireless communication; IoT (Internet of thing) capabilities enable cloud-based modification to adjust to dynamic design requirements. Leveraging Amazon Web Services cloud-based servers, a digital twin of the robotic arm will be developed to assist the project's life cycle, from design to evaluation and test. AWS IoT communication protocols enable near real-time transmission of robotic arm sensor data to its digital twin. Siemens NX CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) facilitates photorealistic physics-based simulation, optimizing robotic arm control and motion planning. The paper details the digital engineering implementation of a two-degree-of-freedom robotic arm featuring piezoelectric rotary motors, applied in a zero gravity simulation air-bearing table study.

results.title: Multifidelity Framework for Small Satellite Thermal Analysis
results.abstract: Anomalies, unexpected events, and model inaccuracies have detrimental effects on satellite operations. High-fidelity models are required, but these models quickly become large and expensive. Cheap or low-fidelity models speed up computation but lack accuracy. To compromise these requirements, this study proposes a multifidelity framework based on cokriging. The proposed multifidelity framework is compared against three other standard methods often used in satellite simulations: a standalone gated recurrent unit, Gaussian process regression, and the autoregressive integrated moving average with explanatory variables model. The robustness of high-fidelity data point placement is also examined. Moreover, the real-time aspect of the simulation is considered by applying the sliding window technique. This multifidelity framework is demonstrated using temperature data obtained from thermal vacuum testing of Small Demonstration Satellite 4: a 50-kg-class satellite. The multifidelity framework provided higher accuracy and robustness than the other methods, however, having a higher computational cost as compared to a purely low-fidelity model. Up to 92% reduction of the error was achieved by the proposed framework.
